bilinear_self_duality_theorem.bilinear_reduction: the Cycle-123 operator is, up to X^epsilon separated terms and power-negligible error, sum_(ell~K) T_1(ell)T_alpha(ell)
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.boundary: self-duality is scoped to tensor separation plus Cauchy and diagonal second moments; it does not exclude correlated bilinear cancellation or prove simple-root closure, a complete moment, density, or intervals
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.cauchy_target: if sum|T_1|^2 and sum|T_alpha|^2 are both O(KDQ X^epsilon), Cauchy gives O(KDQ X^epsilon), exactly the Cycle-87 target
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.inverse: if one separated bilinear term exceeds L*K*D*Q, then at least one of its two normalized second moments exceeds diagonal size by a factor at least L, yielding a labelled pair-collision energy witness
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.mode_change: a=u,b=u+v, alpha=q0/p0; the phase is e(-ell n'g^a)e(-ell alpha m g^b)
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.polynomial: T_alpha(ell)=sum_(a,n) w_alpha(a,n;ell)e(-ell alpha n g^a), with a-length D and n-length Q
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.self_duality: T_alpha is the Cycle-87 primal sparse-exponential polynomial with a bounded rational anchor, up to sign, smooth weights, and tensor-frequency shifts; the transform is norm-neutral at the diagonal second-moment level
bilinear_self_duality_theorem.tensor_separation: every fixed smooth compact coupled symbol in (ell/K,n'g^a/Q,alpha m g^b/Q) has, for each epsilon,A>0, a tensor expansion of rank O(X^epsilon), l1 coefficient norm O(X^epsilon), and uniform error O(X^(-A))
